- Standard credits: Used for work where Notion picks the model for you. Each member gets 1,500 Standard credits a month.*
- Select credits: Used for work where you pick the model yourself, or use a Custom Agent that isn’t funded by your workspace. Each member gets 500 Select credits a month.*

* Your included amount may vary depending on your plan and purchase arrangement.

title: Notion vs Obsidian for Solopreneurs: Pick by the Job (2026)
text:
## The short answer

Pick Notion if most of what you track has a status, a due date or a price: content calendars, launch checklists, product lists, a simple sales pipeline. Its databases and its free calendar app do that work, and the Free plan lists unlimited blocks for a single user.

Pick Obsidian if most of what you produce is writing and thinking: research notes, scripts, newsletter drafts, a long-lived idea file. Your notes stay as Markdown files in a folder on your own machine, and the app is free for business use.

...

| Job in a one-person business | Better fit | Why | What decides it (as of October 2026) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Content calendar with statuses | Notion | Database views by date and status; dates show in Notion Calendar | Notion Calendar is free and can show dates from Notion databases |
| Launch or product tracker | Notion | Relations, properties, buttons | Free plan automations are buttons only; custom database automations start on Plus |
| Intake form (feedback, waitlist, sponsor inquiries) | Notion | Forms write straight into a database | Free has basic forms; custom forms on Plus, conditional logic on Business |
| SOP library you’ll reread for years | Obsidian | Plain files outlive any vendor | Notes are Markdown text files in a local folder |
| Research and swipe file | Obsidian | Fast local search, linking between notes | No plan needed; personal and commercial use are free |
| Long-form drafts (scripts, ebooks, newsletters) | Obsidian | Distraction-light editor, files you can open anywhere | Same Markdown files work in any editor |
| Simple tables over your own notes | Either | Obsidian Bases now gives table, list, cards, kanban and map views | Bases is a core plugin; the data stays in your Markdown files |
| Public help page, roadmap or link hub | Notion for speed, Obsidian for a real site | Notion pages can be shared; Obsidian Publish builds a site with custom domain and passwords | Publish is $8 per site per month billed yearly |
| Asking an AI assistant about your notes | Notion if you’ll pay for Business; Obsidian if your AI tool reads local files | Notion AI is a Business feature; Notion MCP lets outside AI apps in | Free and Plus get a limited AI trial only; MCP connects Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT Pro |
| Capturing ideas from your phone | Either, with a caveat for Obsidian | Notion syncs by default; Obsidian needs a sync method | Free iCloud sync is supported only between Apple devices |

...

Databases are the reason to choose Notion. A content calendar is a database with a date, a status and a channel property, and you can view the same rows as a board, a table or a calendar. For a solo operator juggling a newsletter, a product and a video schedule, that is the closest thing to an operations dashboard without building one.

The Free plan is more usable for one person than its name suggests. As of October 2026 it lists unlimited blocks for a solo user, 10 external guests, basic forms and one chart. The limits show up elsewhere: 5 MB per uploaded file and 7 days of page history. If you store video cuts, design files or big PDFs in your workspace, Free won’t hold them. Plus raises uploads to roughly 5 GB per file and history to 30 days.

Calendar is the second strong argument. Notion Calendar is a free app that syncs Google, Outlook and iCloud calendars, and once your workspace is linked, dated items from a Notion database show up as events. You can also attach or create a Notion page from inside an event. If you already book calls through a scheduler, our guide to scheduling tools for solopreneurs covers that side.

The weak spot is AI pricing. Notion’s own help center says Notion AI is available on Business and Enterprise, while Free and Plus users get a limited number of complimentary responses. If you choose Notion mainly for AI, you’re choosing the $20 tier, not the $10 one.

...

## What one person actually pays, October 2026

Most comparisons list plan prices without saying which ones a solo operator would actually buy. The table below prices the realistic setups for one person, collected from the official pricing and help pages on October 19, 2026.

| Setup for one person | Monthly cost | Billed yearly | The limit you’ll hit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Notion Free | $0 | $0 | 5 MB per file, 7-day page history, AI trial only |
| Notion Plus | $10 listed per member | Up to 20% off yearly | Notion AI still trial-only |
| Notion Business (for Notion AI) | $20 listed per member | Up to 20% off yearly | AI usage allowance is included, but premium models use Notion credits |
| Obsidian, no add-ons | $0 | $0 | You handle sync yourself |
| Obsidian + Sync Standard | $5 | $4/month | 1 GB total, 5 MB per file, 1 synced vault, 1 month of history |
| Obsidian + Sync Plus | $10 | $8/month | 10 GB (upgradable to 100 GB), 200 MB per file, 10 vaults, 12 months of history |
| Add Obsidian Publish | +$10 per site | +$8/month per site | One site per subscription |
| Optional Obsidian commercial license | n/a | $50 per user per year | Not required for business use |

Notion’s pricing page lists Plus at $10 and Business at $20 per member a month and says yearly billing saves up to 20%, but it doesn’t label which billing period the headline figure assumes. Check the toggle at checkout before you commit to a year.

title: Notion for Startups: Plans, AI and a Lean Setup
text:
Notion can give an early-stage startup one place for notes, databases and decisions. Start small: connect customer evidence to the experiments it informs. A solo founder can build that manual workflow on Free; collaboration limits and ongoing AI use may change the plan you need.

If you’re looking for the Notion for Startups offer, it currently advertises up to six free months of Business, including monthly AI credits. Eligibility determines whether the offer is one, three or six months. Check those conditions before budgeting for it.

...

## Which Notion plan does a startup need?

Public USD prices checked October 16, 2026

| Plan | Monthly billing | Annual billing | Relevant fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | $0 | Manual solo workspace; limited AI trial. |
| Plus | $12/member/month | $10/member/month; $120/member/year | Team collaboration; AI remains a limited trial. |
| Business | $24/member/month | $20/member/month; $240/member/year | Notion AI and granular database permissions. |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Additional administration and security controls. |

Free has unlimited pages and blocks for individuals, but collaborative blocks are limited with two or more members. Uploads are limited to 5 MB per file and there are ten guest slots. Guests access invited pages; adding a paid member creates a different billing commitment.

Annual figures are per-member commitments, not month-to-month prices. Currency, taxes and workspace availability can differ. Check Notion’s pricing page and the actual checkout before upgrading.

...

The official startup program is a temporary Business-plan offer, separate from the permanent Free plan:

| Advertised offer | Who should check it |
| --- | --- |
| 6 months | Eligible non-paying startups affiliated with a selected Notion startup partner. |
| 3 months | Eligible non-paying startups without that partner affiliation. |
| 1 month | Smaller teams under ten employees, SMBs or service businesses may receive this tier; incomplete company information can also lead to one month. |

Notion asks for a company website, a work-domain email and fewer than 100 employees. The three- and six-month tiers target scalable technology-related products or services. Prior promotions, a paid account or previously paid history can affect eligibility; use the current program requirements and confirm your situation with Notion.

...

## Where Notion AI helps this workflow

Business and Enterprise include ongoing Notion AI usage with allowances; Free and Plus provide limited trials. The startup offer includes monthly AI credits for the approved Business workspace, but does not remove feature-specific usage limits. Choose an upgrade from the step you actually need:

| Feature | Useful input and output | What you still check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic Autofill | Summarize or tag the content of one Evidence page. | It cannot search other pages or the web. Verify the summary against the original note. |
| Notion Agent | Work with selected permitted pages; draft a comparison of the notes you supply. | Review sources and edits. Do not ask it to invent interview evidence or make the founder’s decision. |
| Enterprise Search | Retrieve cited answers from Notion and configured connected apps. | Check citations and connector scope. Despite its name, it is also available on Business; pricing labels it beta. |
| AI Meeting Notes | Transcribe and summarize an interview after participants consent. | Check the transcript and sharing. Desktop can capture system audio; browser/mobile capture differs and may miss remote voices. |

...

Basic Autofill and Custom Agent Autofill are different. Basic Autofill is included on Business and Enterprise and does not use Notion credits. It reads the individual row or page. Custom Agent Autofill can use broader context; the feature documentation specifies Notion-credit usage. For this starter workflow, a manually written summary is enough.

Current AI allowances, checked October 25, 2026: Notion’s credit documentation describes a standard monthly allocation of 1,500 Standard and 500 Select credits per member. Included amounts may vary by plan and purchase arrangement; check Settings → Notion AI → Usage for your workspace. The new system starts October 19 for new Business and Enterprise workspaces, and November 2 for existing ones.

title: Notion vs Obsidian vs Coda for Solo Founders (2026) - The Real AI Operator
text:
I run most of my day-to-day out of Notion, so let’s start there. It’s a cloud-based workspace that mixes documents, databases, and project boards into one block-based editor. Every page is built from the same primitives: text, headings, toggles, tables, databases, embeds. One workspace can hold your wiki, content calendar, CRM, and task board in the same sidebar. Notion shipped an AI assistant in 2024 and folded it into most plans, so the writing features come with the platform now instead of a separate add-on.

Here’s what you need to know: it’s a cloud app, full stop. Your data sits on Notion’s servers, offline mode lasts a few minutes at best, and your bill scales with seats. That’s the trade for having one URL your cofounder, your VA, and your investor can all open without you provisioning anything. In two years I’ve had two outages that actually mattered, and when Notion goes down your whole brain goes down with it.

...

| Feature | Notion | Obsidian | Coda |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storage model | Cloud-only | Local Markdown files | Cloud (with offline editing) |
| Best for | Docs + tasks + wiki in one | Thinking, writing, knowledge base | Operations, trackers, internal tools |
| Pricing entry point | Free / Plus $12 per user per month | Free / Sync $4 per user per month | Free / Pro $10 per Doc Maker per month |
| Offline mode | Limited (recent pages only) | Full.

...

| AI features | Notion AI on every paid plan | Via plugins (Copilot, Smart Connections) | Coda Brain included on Pro |
| Public sharing | Yes (with Notion Sites) | Yes (with Publish add-on) | Yes (free) |

...

| Open data export | CSV / Markdown export | Already Markdown (yours forever) | CSV / Doc export |

...

## Pricing for a one-person company

What you pay boils down to two things: how many people touch the workspace and which features you actually use. Here’s what a solo founder sees in August 2026.

- Notion: Free for personal use. Plus runs $10 per member per month on annual billing ($12 if you go monthly). Most solo folks stay on Free until they hit the file upload cap or need longer page history.
- Obsidian: The desktop app is free on every platform. If you want your iPad and phone to stay in sync, add Obsidian Sync at $4 a month, billed annually.
- Coda: Free for unlimited viewers. Pro is $10 per Doc Maker per month on annual billing. Most solo founders stick with Free because there’s only one of you editing.

The catch nobody mentions upfront: Notion bills per member, including people who just read. Coda bills per Doc Maker. So if you share your workspace with five advisors who only read, Notion charges you for six seats. Coda charges you for one. I set up a Notion workspace for a client a while back and handed out a few guest logins without thinking too hard about it. The bill at the end of the month made me wince.

title: Notion: an AI agent inside your notes that builds the pages, tasks and databases for you
text:
In one line: Notion keeps your notes, docs, task lists and databases in one place, and its Notion Agent can take a job from start to finish inside that workspace (drafting a page, building a task tracker, summarizing a meeting), with a free plan that's generous for one person but only includes a limited trial of the AI, which starts for real at $20 per member a month billed yearly.

...

Most people know Notion as the app for notes, wikis and to-do lists. What's changed is the AI built into it. Notion Agent is a chat you open inside your workspace, and instead of just answering, it does the work: Notion says it can create and edit pages, databases and charts for you, using what's already in your workspace and, if you connect them, apps like Slack and Google Drive. You can also select text on any page and choose Edit with AI to summarize, translate, fix grammar, change the tone or turn rough notes into an outline. Autofill fills in database columns (summaries, keywords) for every row, and you can upload a file in the chat and get back a spreadsheet, PDF or slide deck. The Business plan unlocks full use of AI Meeting Notes (beta), which transcribes and summarizes calls with no bot joining, Enterprise Search across your connected apps and Research Mode for longer reports, plus Custom Agents that run on a schedule or trigger, like answering questions in Slack or sharing project updates. Notion says it doesn't train on your data unless you opt in, and its AI providers keep data for 30 days outside the Enterprise plan.

...

The AI isn't really free, and it isn't on Plus either. Free and Plus both come with a limited number of complimentary AI responses, and once they're used up, Notion asks you to upgrade to Business or Enterprise to keep using AI. Paying for Plus doesn't bring it back. Every AI action counts as a response, including each Try again. Business includes 1,500 Standard credits a month per member (for work where Notion picks the model) and 500 Select credits (when you pick the model, and for Custom Agents you own). Beyond that, extra usage runs on Notion credits, and Custom Agents are free to try, then $10 per 1,000 Notion credits. Pricing is per member, so a team of five on Business is five seats. The free plan has its own limits too: uploads up to 5 MB per file, 7 days of page history, 10 guests, and a limited number of blocks once a second member joins the workspace.
